proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(W=X\cup C\).  For a role state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), and with the assignments inherited from \((x,c)\), define the proof-local conditional kernel
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 :=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(Y=y\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
       \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right).
\]
The sets in this display are disjoint: \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\), while \(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W\) by the definition of a role state.  The conditional kernel is pointwise defined at every assignment considered below because \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\) puts \(\mathbf M\) in the positive discrete class; in particular, each selected conditioning mass under each displayed intervention is strictly positive.

We first prove trace invariance.  At the root \(\rho_0=(X,C)\), the definition of the target gives
\[
 K_{\rho_0,\mathbf M}(y)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
\]
Suppose that a reachable state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) has already been reached.  If a directed edge of \(\Omega\) moves a nonempty bucket intersection \(T\subseteq\bar X\) from treatment to conditioning, then the edge exists only when the Rule--2 separation in \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\) holds.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X\setminus T.
\]
The required disjointness follows from the role partition and from \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  The cited equality is therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 &=P_{\mathbf M}\!\left(Y=y\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\bar X\setminus T=\bar x_{\bar X\setminus T}),
       T=\bar x_T,\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\right)\\
 &=K_{(\bar X\setminus T,\,\bar C\cup T),\mathbf M}(y).
 \end{aligned}
\]
If instead an edge moves a nonempty \(T\subseteq\bar C\) from conditioning to treatment, use the same cited result with
\[
 A_0=Y,\qquad B_0=T,\qquad C_0=\bar C\setminus T,
 \qquad D_0=\bar X.
\]
Reading its equality in the opposite direction gives
\[
 K_{(\bar X,\bar C),\mathbf M}(y)
 =K_{(\bar X\cup T,\,\bar C\setminus T),\mathbf M}(y).
\]
Induction on the finite length of a trace now yields
\[
 K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)=\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 \tag{1}
\]
at every reachable state \(\rho\), pointwise in the transported assignment.

Now suppose Branch-sCIDP succeeds at \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\).  Its sIDP call has outcome set \(A_0=Y\cup\bar C\) and intervention set \(B_0=\bar X\).  These sets are disjoint, and \(A_0\neq\varnothing\) because \(Y\neq\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  Hence \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}soundness}\) applies to the returned formula and gives, for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\),
\[
 F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x).
 \tag{2}
\]
Because the variables are finite and binary, finite additivity and the definition of \(D_\rho\) give
\[
 \sum_{y'\in\{0,1\}^{Y}}
 F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =\sum_{y'}J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)
 =D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0.
 \tag{3}
\]
The last inequality is precisely where positivity is used.  Dividing (2) by (3), then using the elementary definition of conditional probability and (1), yields
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 {\sum_{y'}F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})}
 =K_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c).
\]
Thus the returned observed-law functional identifies, rather than defines, the causal target.  If \(\bar C=\varnothing\), the denominator in (3) is one; if \(X=\varnothing\), the root is still a valid state.  No division is performed on a failed sIDP call, and no conclusion about \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) has entered the argument.

It remains to prove the finite and computational assertions.  A role state is uniquely determined by the subset \(\bar X\subseteq W\), since \(\bar C=W\setminus\bar X\).  Consequently,
\[
 |\Omega|\le 2^{|W|}=2^{|X\cup C|}.
\]
A nonrepeating trace with \(r\) visited states has \(r-1\) edges, so its length is at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\).

For the shared-cache bound, use the deterministic choices specified in \(\mathrm{def{:}shared\text{-}formula\text{-}cache}\).  There are at most \(2^{|W|}\le 2^n\) outer states.  At each state there are at most two directed tests for each of at most \(n\) nonempty buckets.  A manipulated finite mixed graph has \(O(n^2)\) marked adjacencies.  Ancestor closure and the active-path test can be computed by reachability on the finite graph of ordered adjacent-edge states; hence every Rule--2 test, every anterior-set computation, and every bucket or region computation takes \(\operatorname{poly}(n)\) graph operations.  Thus the complete outer role search costs \(O(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n))\).

For the sIDP work, \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}recursion\text{-}structure}\) shows that a cached fixing subproblem is keyed by a requested region \(R\) and a current set \(T_0\) with \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).  The number of such keys is exactly bounded by
\[
 \#\{(R,T_0):R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\}
 =\sum_{T_0\subseteq V}2^{|T_0|}=3^n,
 \tag{4}
\]
because each observed vertex is in exactly one of \(R\), \(T_0\setminus R\), and \(V\setminus T_0\).  The same cited recursion structure says that a deterministic decomposition child is a proper region subset and that a fixing step strictly removes at least one vertex from its current set.  Therefore each key is evaluated once, its graph work consists of at most \(n\) such scans and updates, and all repeated terminal calls retrieve the cached result.  Equation (4) bounds this work by \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n))\), absorbing the outer-search term.  Finally, each marginalization, product, quotient, and assembly operation is stored once as a constant-arity node of the shared formula DAG.  Writing those nodes and their rational-expression labels costs \(O(L_{\mathrm{form}})\) symbolic operations by the definition of \(L_{\mathrm{form}}\).  The total is therefore
\[
 O\!\left(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}}\right),
\]
as claimed.

Assume \(S=\varnothing\).  Conditioning on \(S=\mathbf 1\) is then conditioning on the sure event, so \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)=P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)\).  In this specialization the selected Rule--2 equality of \(\mathrm{lem{:}selected\text{-}rule\text{-}two}\) is the ordinary PAG Rule--2 equality: the selection coordinate is absent from both sides, and the input-free graph manipulation is unchanged.

Suppose first that CIDP succeeds.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\), its run performs a finite sequence of legal Rule--2 moves of nonempty current bucket intersections and reaches a state \(\rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)\) at which its marginal algorithm identifies
\[
 P_{\mathbf M}(Y,\bar C_\star\mid
 \operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star)).
 \tag{5}
\]
Every move in that sequence is an edge in \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\), so \(\rho_\star\) is enumerated by Branch-sCIDP.  The kernel in (5) is identified over the represented positive discrete class.  If the sIDP call at \(\rho_\star\) failed, \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}completeness}\) would say that this same joint kernel is not identified, contradicting (5).  Hence that call succeeds, and Branch-sCIDP succeeds at \(\rho_\star\) or at an earlier state in its deterministic enumeration.

Conversely, suppose Branch-sCIDP succeeds.  The already proved \(\mathrm{thm{:}branch\text{-}soundness}\) supplies an observed-law functional equal to \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)\) throughout the represented model class.  Thus the conditional effect is identified.  Completeness in \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\) implies that CIDP cannot return \(\operatorname{Fail}\), so CIDP also succeeds.  This proves equality of the two decisions.

Finally, let \(F_\rho\) be any successful Branch-sCIDP joint formula and let \(E\) be the joint formula in the successful CIDP run.  Branch soundness and CIDP soundness from \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\) give, on every compatible positive observational law,
\[
 \frac{F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})}
 {\sum_{y'}F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})}
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)
 =\frac{E(y,c;x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})}{\sum_{y'}E(y',c;x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})}.
\]
Thus the two displayed expressions are algebraically equivalent as identifying functionals on the observational-law domain represented by \(\mathcal P\).  When \(C=\varnothing\), both denominators reduce to one, so the same argument includes the marginal boundary case.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be an input-free COPAG and \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  For pairwise disjoint observed sets \(A_0,B_0,C_0,D_0\subseteq V\), if the Rule--2 separation
\[
 A_0\mathrel{\perp_{\mathsf{id}}}I_{B_0}\mid B_0\cup C_0\cup D_0
 \quad\text{in the graph manipulated by }\operatorname{do}(I_{B_0},D_0)
\]
holds, then, pointwise at every positive discrete assignment,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &P_{\mathbf M}(A_0=a_0\mid C_0=c_0,
       \operatorname{do}(B_0=b_0,D_0=d_0),S=\mathbf 1)\\
 &\qquad =P_{\mathbf M}(A_0=a_0\mid B_0=b_0,C_0=c_0,
       \operatorname{do}(D_0=d_0),S=\mathbf 1).
 \end{aligned}
\]

Let \(\mathcal P\) be an input-free COPAG, let \(A_0,B_0\subseteq V\) be disjoint with \(A_0\neq\varnothing\), and let \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  If \(\operatorname{sIDP}(\mathcal P;A_0,B_0,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) returns a functional \(H(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), then
\[
 H(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =P_{\mathbf M}(A_0\mid\operatorname{do}(B_0),S=\mathbf 1)
\]
for every represented model \(\mathbf M\), including every permitted choice made by the algorithm.

source.locator: Theorem 4.14(1), soundness up to oracle choices

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mathcal P\) be an input-free COPAG and let \(A_0,B_0\subseteq V\) be disjoint with \(A_0\neq\varnothing\).  If \(\operatorname{sIDP}(\mathcal P;A_0,B_0,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) returns \(\operatorname{Fail}\), then \(P_{\mathbf M}(A_0\mid\operatorname{do}(B_0),S=\mathbf 1)\) is not identified over \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).

source.locator: Theorem 4.15, sIDP completeness for input-free COPAGs

added_lemmas.statement: For a fixed deterministic choice rule, sIDP first decomposes every requested observed region only into proper region children.  At a terminal region \(R\), its fixing routine has a current set \(T_0\supseteq R\) and every successful iteration removes a nonempty bucket from \(T_0\).  Consequently every graph-only recursive or fixing subproblem is determined by either a region \(R\subseteq V\) or a pair \(R\subseteq T_0\subseteq V\).

When \(S=\varnothing\), CIDP exchanges only nonempty intersections of the current treatment or conditioning set with a bucket, and only when the corresponding PAG Rule--2 separation holds.  On success it reaches a role state \(\rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)\), identifies \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y,\bar C_\star\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star))\) by its marginal algorithm, and normalizes that joint functional.  CIDP is sound and complete for identification of \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X),C)\) from an input-free PAG.

proposed.statement: Every symbolic formula returned by \(\operatorname{Branch\text{-}sCIDP}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) equals \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). The role graph has at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}\) states, every nonrepeating trace has length at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\), and the shared formula DAG can be constructed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}})\) symbolic operations. No implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification is asserted here.
proposed.justification: Exhaustive legal exchanges preserve the target and isolate the converse difficulty without sacrificing a usable positive identification procedure.
proposed.gap: Chen--Mooij prove soundness for their conditional procedure; the branch closure and shared-cache accounting are not stated as this explicit formula-search theorem.
proposed.consumer: PAGId can return selected-cohort formulas with a finite auditable role trace even before a complete failure theorem is available.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the published selected Rule--2 equality and sIDP soundness theorem used by the proof as explicit load-bearing leaves.

proposed.statement: When \(S=\varnothing\), Branch-sCIDP and CIDP agree on the identification decision for \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)\), and every successful Branch-sCIDP formula is algebraically equivalent to a CIDP identifying functional.
proposed.justification: The no-selection special case is the required regression against the settled conditional-PAG boundary.
proposed.gap: This is a sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim; it rules out a selected extension that changes the established no-selection answer.
proposed.consumer: PAGId retains its current CIDP behavior whenever no selection node is present.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the no-selection CIDP contract, sIDP completeness, Rule--2 specialization, and reachable-role definition used by the regression proof.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the affine family in \(\text{def:affine-mechanism-family}\).  A complete latent-and-endogenous assignment under any fixed observational or interventional regime contains exactly one entry of the varied local table, unless the varied variable is intervened upon, in which case it contains none.  Thus, in the former case, its mass has the form
\[
 \bigl(\theta_j+t v_j\bigr)\prod_{\ell\ne j}p_\ell
 =p_0+t\dot p,
\]
and in the latter case its mass is constant in \(t\).  Marginalization is a finite sum, so there are rational coefficients \(\dot o_z,\dot Z_o,\dot h,\dot k,\dot Z_x\) for which
\[
\begin{aligned}
 o_z(t)&=o_z(0)+t\dot o_z,&
 Z_o(t)&=Z_o(0)+t\dot Z_o,\\
 h(t)&=h(0)+t\dot h,&
 k(t)&=k(0)+t\dot k,&
 Z_x(t)&=Z_x(0)+t\dot Z_x.
\end{aligned}
\]
This uses only the single-table form of \(\text{def:affine-mechanism-family}\).  Strict positivity at \(t=0\), from \(\text{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}\), implies \(Z_o(0)>0\), \(Z_x(0)>0\), and \(h(0)>0\).

For any \(t\) for which the perturbed mechanisms remain positive, direct cross-multiplication gives, for every observed assignment \(z\),
\[
 \frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)}-\frac{o_z(0)}{Z_o(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_o(0)\dot o_z-o_z(0)\dot Z_o\}}
 {Z_o(t)Z_o(0)}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Likewise, using the definitions of \(D_\rho\) and \(N_\rho\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-D_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 &=\frac{h(t)}{Z_x(t)}-\frac{h(0)}{Z_x(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot h-h(0)\dot Z_x\}}
 {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)},                                      \tag{2}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-N_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 &=\frac{k(t)}{Z_x(t)}-\frac{k(0)}{Z_x(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot k-k(0)\dot Z_x\}}
 {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)}.                                      \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
There is no omitted quadratic term in these identities: the products of the two slopes cancel.  Directional coefficients depend linearly on \(v\).  With \(v=R_Tq\), the braces in (1) for all \(z\), followed by the brace in (2), are exactly the coordinates of \(E_Tq\), while the brace in (3) is \(b_Tq\), by \(\text{def:affine-rank-system}\).

We next prove the rank equivalence over \(\mathbb Q\).  If \(b_T\) lies in the row span of \(E_T\), then it vanishes on \(\ker(E_T)\), so no \(q\) of the stated kind exists.  Conversely, suppose that \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  The rule
\[
 \lambda(E_Tq)=b_Tq
\]
is then a well-defined rational linear functional on \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\): two preimages differ by an element of \(\ker(E_T)\).  Extending \(\lambda\) to the ambient rational coordinate space gives \(b_T=\lambda E_T\), so \(b_T\) lies in the row span of \(E_T\).  Therefore
\[
 \bigl(\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}:E_Tq=0,\ b_Tq\ne0\bigr)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 b_T\notin\operatorname{row}(E_T)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T).                           \tag{4}
\]
Rational row reduction both decides (4) and, when it holds, returns a rational null-space vector \(q\) on which \(b_T\) is nonzero.

The condition is intrinsic to the tangent direction and not to its coordinates.  Indeed, if \(R'_T\) is another rational basis matrix for \(T\), then \(R'_T=R_TH\) for an invertible rational matrix \(H\).  Consequently
\[
 ER'_T=E_TH,\qquad bR'_T=b_TH.
\]
Right multiplication by \(H\) preserves both ranks in (4), and \(q\mapsto H^{-1}q\) preserves the represented direction \(v\).  This proves basis independence.

Let the returned direction be \(v=R_Tq\).  Since \(b_Tq\ne0\), one has \(v\ne0\).  Define
\[
 \delta=\frac12\min_{j:v_j\ne0}
 \left\{\frac{\theta_j}{|v_j|},
              \frac{1-\theta_j}{|v_j|}\right\}.       \tag{5}
\]
Every number in the minimum is a positive rational number by \(\text{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}\), so \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) and it is computable.  Because \(v\in T\), the entries of \(v\) sum to zero within each probability block.  Hence \(\theta+t v\) remains normalized.  If \(0<|t|<\delta\), (5) also gives, coordinatewise,
\[
 0<\theta_j-|t|\,|v_j|
 \le \theta_j+t v_j
 \le \theta_j+|t|\,|v_j|<1.                            \tag{6}
\]
Thus every rational \(t\) in this punctured interval produces another strictly positive rational mechanism.  All other local tables are unchanged, so \(\mathbf M(0),\mathbf M(t)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\) by \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\).  Positivity also makes every denominator in (1)--(3) positive.

Now take \(\mathbf M_0=\mathbf M(0)\) and \(\mathbf M_1=\mathbf M(t)\).  The equality \(E_Tq=0\), (1), and (2) imply
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1},
 \qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}>0.         \tag{7}
\]
The inequality \(b_Tq\ne0\), (3), and \(t\ne0\) imply
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}\ne N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}.       \tag{8}
\]
Therefore the two terminal conditional probabilities, equal respectively to \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}/D_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}\), are different.  The graphical data supplied to \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) satisfy the represented-forest clauses in \(\text{def:locked-certificate}\), and its supplied legal role trace is a sequence of Rule--2 action--observation exchanges.  Each such exchange preserves the conditional kernel on the positive stratum; composing the equalities along the finite trace transfers the terminal disagreement to \(\psi_{\mathbf M_0}\ne\psi_{\mathbf M_1}\).  Together with (7), this contradicts the implication in \(\text{def:identification}\).  Hence the compiled pair certifies nonidentification of \(\psi\).

It remains to justify the computational assertions.  Let \(m\) and \(r\) be the row and column dimensions of the explicitly encoded rational matrix, and let \(B\) bound its input bit lengths.  Clearing denominators followed by fraction-free elimination uses polynomially many integer operations.  Every intermediate pivot is a minor of an integerized input matrix; the Leibniz expansion bounds an \(s\)-by-\(s\) minor by \(s!\) times the product of \(s\) input bounds, hence its bit length is \(O(s(B+\log s))\).  Thus the rank test and a rational null vector have bit complexity polynomial in the explicit matrix encoding, which is part of \(L_{\mathrm{temp}}\).  Formula (5) and a choice such as \(t=\delta/2\) require only polynomially many exact rational operations.

The compiler copies the supplied graph, trace, and forest coordinates and enumerates the dense assignment tables.  Each table entry is a product of at most the number of vertices many encoded local probabilities, and each marginal is a sum over entries that are themselves written in the expanded output.  Exact construction therefore costs a polynomial in \(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma}\), including the time needed to write the output.  For verification, acyclicity, ancestry, endpoint compatibility, the role trace, and the forest predicates are finite graph reachability or local-incidence checks; the represented latent-projection and separation claims can be checked by graph search on the standard polynomial-size state graph of vertex and incoming-edge-mark pairs.  The verifier then checks block normalization and strict positivity, recomputes every displayed observational and interventional atom from the dense rational factorization tables, and checks (7)--(8) by exact cross-multiplication.  The number and bit length of all checked entries are bounded by \(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma}\), and sequential rational products and sums have polynomial bit growth in that expanded encoding.  Hence both compilation and verification have the claimed polynomial bit complexity.

All variables in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are binary.  The displayed local success probabilities and their complements belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac14,\frac12,\frac34,
              \frac5{16},\frac7{16},\frac9{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\},
\]
so every local entry is rational and strictly between zero and one.  The table for \(X_i\) changes with \(U_i\); the table for \(Y_i\) changes with each of \(X_i\) and \(U_i\); the table for \(C_i\) changes with \(Y_i\); and the table for \(S_i\) changes with each of \(Y_i\) and \(C_i\).  Thus the parent relations are exactly those of \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

Marginalizing \(U_i\) produces the directed edge \(X_i\to Y_i\) and the bidirected edge \(X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\) induced by \(X_i\leftarrow U_i\to Y_i\); the other displayed arrows have no latent internal vertex and remain.  No further latent-projection edge is created because every other path has an observed internal vertex.  This is precisely \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\).  In the selected projection onto \(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), all three observed vertices are ancestors of \(S_i\), so the adjacent endpoint marks are tails.  The pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) and \((Y_i,C_i)\) are adjacent, whereas \(X_i\) and \(C_i\) are separated by \(\{Y_i\}\) conditional on \(S_i\): in the ancestral moral graph for \(\{X_i,C_i,Y_i,S_i\}\), removing the conditioned vertices \(Y_i,S_i\) leaves \(C_i\) disconnected from the component containing \(X_i\).  Hence the observed MAG is exactly the undirected noncollider chain
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i.
\]
The three-node noncollider equivalence class has no invariant endpoint mark, so its input-free completed partial graph is \(X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\).  This proves
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}),
 \quad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M},
 \quad \mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}.
\]
Together with positivity, rationality, and binary support, \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\) gives
\(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+},\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}
\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\).

We now calculate the laws.  Since \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(X_i=1)&=\tfrac12\tfrac14+\tfrac12\tfrac34=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=1)&=\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac34=r_1,\\
 P(X_i=0)&=\tfrac12\tfrac34+\tfrac12\tfrac14=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=0)&=\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac14=r_0.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{9}
\]
Thus, for \(a\in\{0,1\}\), iterated expectation and the outcome table give
\[
 P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)
 =\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
   \{P(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)-r_a\}=\frac12.                \tag{10}
\]
For every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\), multiplication of the \(C_i\) and \(S_i\) tables yields
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 (b,d)&(0,0)&(0,1)&(1,0)&(1,1)\\ \hline
 P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)
 &(3/4)(1/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(3/4)(1/4)
\end{array}
=\frac3{16}.                                             \tag{11}
\]
Combining \(P(X_i=a)=1/2\), (10), and (11),
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac3{16}=\frac3{64}.       \tag{12}
\]
Summing (12) over the eight observed cells gives \(P_\sigma(S_i=1)=3/8\), and division gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d\mid S_i=1)
 =\frac{3/64}{3/8}=\frac18.                              \tag{13}
\]
The selected observational laws are therefore identical and have full support.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), the intervention deletes the \(U_i\to X_i\) factor but leaves \(U_i\) fair.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_+(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12+\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac9{16},\\
 P_-(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12-\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac7{16}.       \tag{14}
\end{aligned}
\]
Equation (11) gives \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) and therefore
\[
 P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=\sum_{d=0}^1\frac3{16}=\frac38.     \tag{15}
\]
It follows from (14)--(15) that each interventional selection normalizer is \(3/8\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=\frac{\sum_b P_\sigma(Y_i=b\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))(3/16)}{3/8}
 =\frac12,                                                \tag{16}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac{(9/16)(3/16)}{3/8}=\frac9{32},                  \tag{17}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac{(7/16)(3/16)}{3/8}=\frac7{32}.                  \tag{18}
\end{aligned}
\]
The positive common denominator in (16) turns (17)--(18) into conditional effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\).  Also, directly from the \(C_i\) table,
\[
 P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=\frac34\ne\frac14=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0),
\]
so the conditioning coordinate is genuinely informative before selection.

For the graphical obstruction, \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is bidirected-connected, every vertex has at most one directed child, and its unique childless root is \(Y_i\).  The singleton \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is a proper C-subforest with the same root.  Directly,
\[
 V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\},\qquad
 V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing.
\]
After intervening on \(X_i\), the root \(Y_i\) is still an ancestor of the terminal set \(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}\), indeed it is a member of that set and has directed paths to \(C_i\) and \(S_i\).  Thus
\[
 R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}
 (\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}).                                     \tag{19}
\]
There is no intervention-input vertex, so the maximal selection-exchange coordinate for this terminal query is \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\).  The bidirected connectivity, common-root, treatment-intersection, ancestry, and empty-exchange checks above are exactly the terminal selected-hedge predicates in \(\text{def:informative-graph-certificate}\).  Hence \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) is the asserted terminal selected hedge.

Finally modify only the cell \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\).  The changed selection table remains strictly positive and still depends on both parents.  Equations (9)--(10) are unchanged, so both signs have the same unselected observed law; the common modified \(C_i,S_i\) mechanisms then imply the same full selected observational law for both signs.  If
\(p=P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))\), the modified table gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac38+p\frac9{16}=\frac{6+3p}{16},\\
 P(C_i=1,S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac3{16}+p\frac38=\frac{3+3p}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the modified denominator is
\[
 \widetilde D_\sigma=\frac{1+p}{2+p}.
\]
Substitution of \(p=9/16\) and \(p=7/16\) from (14) yields
\[
 \widetilde D_+=\frac{25}{41},\qquad
 \widetilde D_-=\frac{23}{39},
\]
which are unequal.  The original equality (16) is therefore an exact cancellation of the informative mechanisms, not a consequence of the represented graph.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The missing implication is from failure of the terminal sIDP call at every reachable role state to a represented residual forest carrying either a rational one- or two-mechanism tangent with \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\ne0\), or an alternative explicit denominator-locked positive rational model pair, together with synthesis in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.
open_obligations.obstruction: Unconditional sIDP failure can supply a terminal-joint obstruction, but it does not force two observationally equivalent models to have the same selected conditioning denominator. Algebraically, nonidentification of the joint does not imply that the numerator row lies outside the row span of the observational and denominator lock rows. No frozen result coordinates this rank-separation property across all reachable role states or all represented residual forests.
open_obligations.attempted: The residual-forest handle was reduced to the exact one-mechanism rank test, and the same reduction suggests enlarging to a two-mechanism tangent when the first test fails. The explicit informative selected bow shows that a connected conditioning coordinate can pass the lock, while ratio-cancellation examples show why failure of a particular terminal joint is insufficient. What remains unproved is the exhaustive graphical dichotomy asserting that every all-branches-fail COPAG yields a passing finite rational template; neither the one-mechanism test nor an unspecified two-mechanism enlargement proves that coverage.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For any supplied rational interior one-mechanism template, the exact condition
\[
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T)
\]
is necessary and sufficient for that template to yield a positive rational pair with identical full selected observational law, identical positive terminal denominator, and different terminal numerator; such a pair is compilable and verifiable in polynomial time in its explicit input and output lengths.  The informative three-observed-vertex construction supplies one represented terminal forest for which the locked pair exists even though the conditioning variable is connected and informative.  These results do not establish that every residual forest produced by universal branch failure admits such a one- or two-mechanism direction.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\) and \(a,d\in\{0,1\}\).  By the SCM factorization for the DAG \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{iso}}\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}isolated\mbox{-}bow\mbox{-}template}\),
\[
 P_{\sigma}(u,x,y,c,s)
 =P(u)P(c)P(x\mid u)P_{\sigma}(y\mid x,u)P(s\mid y).
\]
All displayed local probabilities in that definition are rational and lie strictly between zero and one.  In particular, the four possible outcome-mechanism values belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac{5}{16},\frac{7}{16},\frac{9}{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\}.
\]
Thus every cell needed below is positive, the conditioning operations are legitimate, and, together with Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}binary\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}support}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}rational\mbox{-}interior\mbox{-}mechanisms}\), the two models have the stipulated positive rational binary support.

The treatment marginal is fair:
\[
 P(X_b=1)
 =\frac12\frac14+\frac12\frac34
 =\frac12,
 \qquad
 P(X_b=0)
 =\frac12\frac34+\frac12\frac14
 =\frac12.
\]
Bayes' formula may therefore be applied with a positive denominator, and it gives
\[
 P(U_b=1\mid X_b=0)
 =\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}
 =\frac14=r_0^b,
 \qquad
 P(U_b=1\mid X_b=1)
 =\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}
 =\frac34=r_1^b.
\]
Consequently, using the outcome mechanism from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}isolated\mbox{-}bow\mbox{-}template}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}(u-r_a^b)\right\}
 P(U_b=u\mid X_b=a)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
 \left\{P(U_b=1\mid X_b=a)-r_a^b\right\}\\
 &=\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(C_b\) is an isolated fair root in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{iso}}\), the factorization gives \(P(C_b=d)=1/2\) and makes \(C_b\) independent of \((X_b,Y_b,S_b)\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=1,S_b=1)
 &=P(X_b=a)P(C_b=d)
   P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a)P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=1)\\
 &=\frac12\frac12\frac12\frac23
 =\frac1{12},\\
 P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=0,S_b=1)
 &=P(X_b=a)P(C_b=d)
   P_{\sigma}(Y_b=0\mid X_b=a)P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=0)\\
 &=\frac12\frac12\frac12\frac13
 =\frac1{24}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing these cells over the two values of \(a\) and the two values of \(d\) yields
\[
 P_{\sigma}(S_b=1)
 =4\left(\frac1{12}+\frac1{24}\right)
 =\frac12.
\]
It follows, cell by cell, that
\[
 P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=y\mid S_b=1)
 =
 \begin{cases}
  1/6,&y=1,\\
  1/12,&y=0,
 \end{cases}
\]
which is independent of \(\sigma\).  Since the binary cells indexed by \((a,d,y)\) exhaust the observed sample space, the two full selected observational laws agree.

Now intervene to set \(X_b=0\).  The truncated SCM factorization leaves the fair root \(U_b\) unchanged.  Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p_{\sigma}
 &:=P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))\\
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left\{\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}\left(u-\frac14\right)\right\}P(U_b=u)\\
 &=\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)
 =\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
 p_{+}=\frac9{16},
 \qquad
 p_{-}=\frac7{16}.
\]
The selection mechanism depends only on \(Y_b\), so its postintervention normalizer is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Z_{\sigma}
 &:=P_{\sigma}(S_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))\\
 &=\frac23p_{\sigma}+\frac13(1-p_{\sigma})
 =\frac{1+p_{\sigma}}3.
\end{aligned}
\]
It follows that
\[
 Z_{+}=\frac{25}{48},
 \qquad
 Z_{-}=\frac{23}{48},
\]
both of which are positive.  Take the terminal role state with \(\bar X=\{X_b\}\), \(\bar C=\{C_b\}\), outcome \(Y_b\), and assignments \(\bar x=0\), \(\bar c=1\).  Isolation of \(C_b\) is preserved by the intervention, and hence the selected terminal joint kernel is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac{P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1,C_b=1,S_b=1
       \mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))}{Z_{\sigma}}\\
 &=\frac{p_{\sigma}(1/2)(2/3)}{Z_{\sigma}}
 =\frac{p_{\sigma}}{1+p_{\sigma}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution gives the two claimed joint numerators,
\[
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},+}}(1,1;0)=\frac9{25},
 \qquad
 J_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},-}}(1,1;0)=\frac7{23}.
\]
Moreover, the same isolation factorization gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=P_{\sigma}(C_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0),S_b=1)\\
 &=\frac{P(C_b=1)P_{\sigma}(S_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))}{Z_{\sigma}}\\
 &=\frac{(1/2)Z_{\sigma}}{Z_{\sigma}}
 =\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\]
The division is valid because \(Z_{\sigma}>0\).  Normalizing the selected joint kernel by this denominator therefore yields
\[
 P_{\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},+}}(Y_b=1\mid
 \operatorname{do}(X_b=0),C_b=1,S_b=1)
 =\frac{9/25}{1/2}=\frac{18}{25},
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},-}}(Y_b=1\mid
 \operatorname{do}(X_b=0),C_b=1,S_b=1)
 =\frac{7/23}{1/2}=\frac{14}{23}.
\]
Finally, the equation \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\sigma}}(1;0)=1/2\) used only that \(C_b\) is an isolated fair root; it did not use cancellation between the sign-indexed outcome mechanisms.  Thus denominator equality is structurally automatic in this baseline, establishing precisely why the example is vacuous as evidence for generic denominator locking.
